quests.conceptTitle: Pre-Reading Schema Activation: Mangroves and Storms
quests.passage: Mangrove forests grow along tropical coasts, their tangled roots rising out of salty mud. Those roots slow incoming waves, so a belt of mangroves can reduce a wave's force before it reaches the shore. After a severe cyclone struck one coastal region, villages sheltered by mangroves reported far less flooding than neighboring villages without them. Mangroves also trap sediment, which gradually builds up the land, and they provide nurseries for young fish. Despite these benefits, many forests have been cleared for shrimp farms, leaving communities more exposed.

quests.passage: When Dario opened the envelope, the number on the slip was smaller than he'd calculated. He had counted the hours, multiplied, and then forgotten that taxes would be taken out first. Next time, you'll know what to expect." Dario folded it carefully and put it in his wallet instead of the bin.

quests.passage: Rental companies usually offer two levels of cover. Basic cover costs $12 a day and includes theft protection, but the driver pays the first $1,500 of any damage. Full cover costs $28 a day and reduces that amount to zero. Many credit cards already include some rental insurance, so it is worth checking before you pay for extra cover. For a short trip on quiet country roads, basic cover may be enough; for a week in heavy city traffic, many drivers feel the extra $16 a day is worth the peace of mind.

quests.passageTopic: Why I Stopped Checking Email Constantly
quests.passage: For years I checked my inbox every few minutes, convinced that fast replies made me a better colleague. Then I tracked my day and found that I spent nearly two hours on email, most of it in small interruptions that broke up my real work. Now I check three times a day, at nine, noon, and four, and I add a line to my signature explaining why. Nobody has complained. A few people have even copied the idea, which was not why I did it, but I admit it feels good.

quests.conceptTitle: Pre-Reading Schema Activation: Harbor at Dawn
quests.passage: By half past five, the harbor had begun to stir. Fishing crews moved along the quay in the gray light, hauling crates and calling to one another in short, practiced phrases. Gulls circled above the boats, waiting for scraps. The café at the end of the pier had just switched on its lights, and the smell of fresh coffee drifted over the water. Nobody hurried; the work had a rhythm that came from repetition. Only the tourists, who would not arrive for hours, would later describe the scene as peaceful. For those inside it, it was simply morning.
